subfamily: gin Old-Fashioned, built over ice, after the Codex root recipe (p. 5: spirit, sugar, bitters)
glass: plain kitchen tumbler (about 250 ml), three or four ordinary ice cubes from the freezer tray
version: v0 (Tomás, round 2, 2026-10-01). Tanqueray London Dry, recommended (any juniper-led London dry gin, 40-47.3%). Spark: the sugar is a licorice root syrup. Licorice is purportedly one of Tanqueray's four botanicals (juniper, coriander, angelica, licorice) and Oxford hears 'just a hint of licorice' in its finish (TANQUERAY GORDON & CO. pdf 1986): the syrup brings forward what's already in the bottle, it doesn't dress it. Sweep: 40% 27.8%/7.0 g, 43.1% 29.9%/7.0 g in range; 47.3% 32.8% edge (50 ml lands 31.9%/8.1 g). Sugar held under Arnold's 7.6 g because glycyrrhizin reads sweeter than its grams (unsourced). Licorice root classed nuts on the safe side (legume, kin to peanut; dried roots often packed with nuts): the pour leaves veto-free.
